stories.headline: TCB set to boost essential goods trade with Pakistan's TCP
stories.summary: On 14 January 2025, Pakistan's TCP and Bangladesh's Directorate General of Food signed a government-to-government MoU allowing Pakistan to export up to 200,000 tonnes of rice annually to Bangladesh. At the ninth meeting of the Joint Economic Commission on 27 October 2025, the Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution and the Pakistan Halal Authority signed another MoU to expand halal product trade.

The proposed agreement comes as TCB plans to procure essential commodities worth around Tk8,000 crore in FY27 to maintain supplies for low-income consumers.

stories.headline: BIWTA to seek more time from HC to remove plastic waste from Buriganga
stories.summary: The Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA) will seek more time from the High Court (HC) as it could not completely remove plastic bottles and other plastic waste from Buriganga riverbank within the deadline of December 14, as directed by the court. Mobarak Hossain Mazumder said that BIWTA had identified 220 plastic recycling factories located within two kilometres of both banks of the Buriganga River in Lalbagh area of the capital, which are also responsible for river pollution.

stories.exam_facts: He said that around 2.5 million people live in the Lalbagh area, discharging solid and liquid waste into the river, contributing significantly to its pollution. Earlier on November 8 this year, the High Court directed the BIWTA and other authorities concerned to completely remove plastic wastes from the banks of the Buriganga River in Islampur, under Lalbagh and Kamrangirchar areas in the capital.

stories.headline: Human rights, labour standards made central to FTA
stories.summary: Bangladesh exported goods worth 23.3 billion euros to the EU in 2025, making the European market crucial to its macroeconomic stability. The European Union is ready to match Bangladesh's ambition for a free-trade agreement (FTA), with exploratory discussions between the two sides scheduled to begin next month, as Brussels seeks to elevate its relationship with Dhaka into a broader strategic partnership.

stories.exam_facts: The decision was made at a meeting of the bank's board of directors on Sunday, according to a corporate disclosure issued to investors on the stock exchanges today (23 November). In 2025, the bank reported a profit of Tk336.33 crore and paid an 8% cash dividend and a 5% stock dividend to its shareholders.

stories.headline: Bangladesh, UK discuss climate investment, Rohingya repatriation
stories.summary: British High Commissioner to Bangladesh Sarah Cooke met State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today (23 November), according to a press release from the ministry. Cooke informed Shama Obaed about the UK's inaugural contribution of £400 million to a new mechanism under the Climate Investment Funds (CIF), aimed at boosting private investment in clean energy.
stories.why_it_matters: Key fact to remember: British High Commissioner to Bangladesh Sarah Cooke met State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today (23 November), according to a press release from the ministry. stories.exam_facts: Bangladesh, UK discuss climate investment, Rohingya repatriation Bangladesh and the United Kingdom have discussed expanding cooperation on climate investment and ensuring the safe repatriation of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar. They also discussed attracting more climate investment to Bangladesh and expanding cooperation on early warning systems, climate displacement, the effects of climate change on women and children, and promoting eco-friendly natural fibres such as jute.
